page: UpCloud PREMIUM-16xCPU-32GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a cache hierarchy containing 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. Local storage is bundled as a 300 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Conversely, multi-core operations, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register average performance, as do database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Large language model inference speeds are average for prompt processing and medium-model text generation, though text generation on smaller models registers in the bottom 10%.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as a compute-heavy resource, offering high compute density relative to its memory footprint. While single-threaded tasks excel due to the underlying AMD EPYC architecture, the shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for sustained, multi-core workloads that require dedicated execution resources. Qualitatively, the server provides a cost-efficient entry point for compute-intensive tasks that do not demand massive memory allocations. It is well-suited for workloads such as single-threaded data processing, web serving, moderate database operations, and lightweight compilation tasks.
